\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]

(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let

\[
a=\frac yx,\qquad b=\frac zy,\qquad c=\frac xz.
\]

Then \(a,b,c>0\) and \(abc=1\). Also,

\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=xyz(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=3(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=40,
\]

so

\[
(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=\frac{40}{3}.
\]

Similarly,

\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)=xyz(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=3(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=4,
\]

so

\[
(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Let

\[
S=a+b+c,\qquad T=ab+bc+ca.
\]

Since \(abc=1\),

\[
(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=1+S+T+1=S+T+2=\frac{40}{3},
\]

and

\[
(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=1-S+T-1=T-S=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Thus

\[
S+T=\frac{34}{3},\qquad T-S=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Solving gives

\[
S=5,\qquad T=\frac{19}{3}.
\]

So \(a,b,c\) are the roots of

\[
t^3-5t^2+\frac{19}{3}t-1=0,
\]

or

\[
3t^3-15t^2+19t-3=(t-3)(3t^2-6t+1)=0.
\]

Hence

\[
\{a,b,c\}=\left\{3,\;1+\frac{\sqrt6}{3},\;1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right\}.
\]

Now

\[
y=ax,\qquad z=abx,
\]

so

\[
3=xyz=x(ax)(abx)=a^2b\,x^3.
\]

Therefore

\[
x^3=\frac{3}{a^2b}=\frac{3c}{a}.
\]

To minimize \(x\), we minimize \(x^3\). Among the three possible values for \(a\) and \(c\), the smallest value of \(\frac{3c}{a}\) occurs when \(a=3\) and \(c=1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\). This gives

\[
x^3=1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}}}.
\]
